perf.summary: Sequential prefix-sum has a loop-carried dependency that blocks vectorization; acceptable but flaggable.
perf.currentCost: `cur += diff[i]; dst[i]=cur;` carries a dependency through `cur`, so Burst cannot auto-vectorize the scan; throughput is one add per cycle at best.
perf.proposedChange: Leave as-is for small len (dependency chain is cheap and code is clear). For large len only, a two-pass blocked/SIMD prefix-sum (partial sums per lane then offset) can be ~2-4x faster, but it adds complexity and a scratch pass — recommend only if profiling shows this is hot.
perf.rationale: Documents the inherent serialization; the blocked-scan trades the dependency chain for parallel partial sums. Constant-factor only, not asymptotic.
perf.risk: Blocked prefix-sum is easy to get wrong (lane offsets, overflow into int). Output must stay int with identical wraparound semantics. Only worth it for large arrays; default keep the simple form.
